ABSENCE: no mention of fail-open vs fail-closed policy, timeout, or circuit-breaker for the blocking decision

findings.finding: The new HIGH-class blocking gate at 0.90 has no specified failure mode — if the routing/scoring system errors, it is undefined whether reviews fail open (allow) or fail closed (block).
findings.location: Approach section: 'blocking_enabled true at 0.90 scoped to the rubric's HIGH classes'; Acceptance Criteria: 'T5c HIGH-class findings at >= 0.90 block'

findings.finding: No observability is specified for when a HIGH-class finding triggers a block — operators cannot tell from metrics, logs, or alerts why a review was blocked or whether the blocking gate is firing correctly.
findings.location: Approach section (blocking_enabled); Testing section

findings.finding: The plan mutates criteria_routing.json (shared config consumed by Pass-3 and potentially other pipeline steps) but does not enumerate all consumers or specify a default/backward-compatible behavior when the new blocking_enabled key is absent in older deployments.

However, the current `plan_review_T5c.md` already contains 'SAME-ROUND DEDUP: emit ONE finding per (surface, defect) pair' in its existing text. The plan positions same-round dedup as novel work when it already exists in the rubric.

The genuinely new work (the one-per-plan cap on undeclared-access-posture specifically, and the demotion rule) is conflated with already-present work, obscuring what actually needs to change.
